stem: If X follows a normal distribution N(mu, sigma^2), what proportion of observations lie within one standard deviation of the mean, i.e., between (mu - sigma) and (mu + sigma)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 99.73% is the coverage for plus-or-minus three standard deviations (the 3-sigma rule), not one sigma.
The empirical rule states that approximately 68.27% of a normal distribution falls within plus-or-minus one standard deviation of the mean.
95.45% is the coverage for plus-or-minus two standard deviations (the 2-sigma rule), not one sigma.
50% is the coverage for zero standard deviations, i.e., exactly at the mean; it corresponds to a degenerate interval and confuses the median property with an interval coverage.

explanation: The empirical 68-95-99.7 rule for normal distributions: approximately 68.27% of data lies within 1 sigma of mu, 95.45% within 2 sigma, and 99.73% within 3 sigma. These come from integrating the standard normal density from -1 to 1, -2 to 2, and -3 to 3 respectively.

explanation_sections.punchline: The 1-sigma interval captures about 68.27% of a normal distribution, not 95% or 99.7%.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the distribution model (normal) and the property tested (empirical rule). Memorise the three thresholds: 1 sigma = 68.27%, 2 sigma = 95.45%, 3 sigma = 99.73%. The question asks for 1 sigma, so select 68.27%.
explanation_sections.lesson: The 68-95-99.7 rule is a fixed property of the normal curve; pair the sigma count with the right percentage before selecting.
explanation_sections.timing: Pure recall, 20-30 seconds. The trap is confusing the three sigma levels; one sigma always gives ~68%.
